Subject: Flicker — intermittent long-tail completions since 04/13

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing a bunch of slow completions and a spike in 5xx error rate on our production app around ~18:30 PDT yesterday. Most traffic looks normal, but about ~2-3% of requests now take 20-40s to finish (p95 jumps to ~21s, p99 to ~37s) and we're also seeing timeouts hitting our client side. Attached are a sample of request ids and traces (flicker_traces_20280413.zip) and a short list of sample requests.

This is impacting checkout flows and one of our key features. Can you please triage urgently and let us know ETA for a mitigation? We have an upcoming marketing push and need a short-term fix plus a plan to prevent re-occurrence.

Thanks,
Elliot

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Chen <eng@flickerlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 23:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Flicker — intermittent long-tail completions since 04/13

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Observed brief period at 18:28-18:46 PDT where Flicker’s routed requests see queue depth grow on a subset of hosts behind the us-west routing pool.
- Concurrency cap for their account was hit on several frontends (we enforce per-tenant concurrency to avoid noisy neighbors). When caps hit, requests are queued at the request router layer; we’re seeing head-of-line blocking where a few straggler completions (large context requests) delay many queued requests.
- KV cache eviction spikes correlate with the same window — likely due to model variants with larger KV footprints getting routed. Eviction causes cache misses that amplify tail time for subsequent requests.
- Error spike (5xx) appears to be transient overload timeouts from the serving runtime for those stragglers; not model failures.

Short-term mitigation we can toggle immediately (low risk):
1) Temporarily raise Flicker Labs’ concurrency cap by 2x in the us-west pool (will increase CPU/GPU pressure but reduces router queuing).
2) Enable sticky routing to smaller-variant instances for the next 30m to avoid KV-footprint churn.
3) Turn on a short-lived circuit-breaker at 10% for very large-context requests to keep them from clogging the queue (return 429 to the client so they can retry lighter).

I can flip 1 & 2 now and coordinate with Elliot to enable 3 if acceptable.

I’ll keep digging; logging a JIRA for deeper postmortem.

- Dev

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Chen <eng@flickerlabs.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation applied — preliminary results and next steps

Update after toggles: we raised Flicker’s concurrency cap in us-west and enabled sticky routing to smaller-variant instances at 15:40 PDT. We also applied the temporary circuit-breaker for >6k context requests.

Preliminary results (15:40–16:30 PDT):
- p95 for routed requests dropped from ~21s to ~3.6s.
- p99 reduced from ~37s to ~7.8s (still elevated vs baseline but much improved).
- 5xx rate returned to baseline; client timeouts cleared.

Next steps (post-sync):
- Engineering will run a tailored load test to reproduce the KV-eviction + straggler pattern and validate a long-term fix (options: smarter KV sharding, proactive warm-place allocation for large-context variants, adaptive per-tenant concurrency tied to observed queue depth). I’ve filed JIRA-INF-2983 for the postmortem and follow-through.
- CS to discuss whether Flicker wants a standing higher concurrency commit while they run their marketing push (commercial concession discussion).
- Ops to add a dashboard panel for per-tenant queue depth and eviction rate to catch regressions earlier (link added to related_links).

Elliot — can you confirm that your ingestion/application timeouts are acceptable now? If you still see outliers, forward more traces and we’ll iterate.

-David
